arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Saunders argued the 2006 Veterans Act requires prioritizing veteran-owned firms. He stated this applies before awarding contracts to other suppliers.
Mr. Tripp argued the mandate applies to wholly new contracts. He stated it does not apply to orders under old contracts.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on federal procurement rules. Kingdomware seeks to enforce a statutory preference. The government defends its current contracting method.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on February 22, 2016.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Kingdomware wants the Court to order the VA to prioritize veteran-owned firms for new orders.
The government wants the Court to allow the VA to place orders under existing contracts.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Kingdomware argues the 2006 Veterans Act mandates prioritizing veteran-owned firms before other suppliers.
The government argues the mandate applies only to wholly new contracts, not existing orders.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 25, lines 52-10

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Kennedy asked about the specific contract amount.

Justice Sotomayor asked if the client remains a Federal Supply Schedule vendor. She also asked about stipulated costs and database capabilities. She questioned if ruling for Kingdomware would eliminate the Federal Supply Schedule system. Justice Alito asked what relief is consistent with the Tucker Act.
